🎉 Birthday dinner recap at @oulacarteret | Carteret, NJ 🍽️

Short clips, big memories, full bellies, and so much love. This reel is just a glimpse into a really beautiful night with people I adore 🖤 

For my birthday, we did a prefix menu, and overall I’d give the experience a 9/10. From start to finish, my guests and I were very well taken care of, which truly matters when you’re celebrating something special 🤍

✨ Apps: 10/10, no debate.
Everything on the ti goute portion of the menu—epis shrimp, griot cups, Haitian meatballs—was absolutely delicious ❤️ We honestly could’ve eaten just that all night. Add the beet salad and soup joumou? Perfection. We truly could’ve stopped there 🥣

🍹 Drinks: beautifully made, well-balanced, and consistent all night 🥂

🍖 Entrees were mixed.
Most of my guests ordered the oxtails and rated them about a 6/10. They were cooked well, but the flavor leaned more toward a clove/black-licorice note than the classic Haitian oxtail taste many of us grew up loving, and the rice wasn’t as savory as I prefer. Not a repeat order for me—but everyone’s palate is different 🤷🏾‍♀️

That said, I would absolutely recommend Ou La, especially for birthdays and group celebrations 🎂💕 I’d love to come back on a regular night to try dishes outside the prefix menu and experience the service in a different setting.

📍 Carteret, NJ
🚗 Free parking in the back (which matters!) 💗

Good food, good drinks, good people, good energy 🥂

NEW YORK: FRIDAY 4/3 Com Truise DJ set at H0L0 🎶

Com Truise is the nom de guerre of producer and graphic designer Seth Haley, born-and-raised in upstate New York. His synth- and sci-fi-obsessed records are as infectious as they are expansive. 

From 2011's Galactic Melt LP to its long-awaited follow-ups, Iteration (2017) and Persuasion System (2019), and assorted EPs, rarities compilations, and remixes in-between, Com Truise has consistently continued to refine his singular style of melodic beat music. Each release ties together his ideas of "synth-wave" and "slow-motion funk" amidst a glowing backdrop of rich, nostalgic pathos.

@sam_branden ｜Alloy
@____chart____ × Pegasus at @lovesclubnyc  Brooklyn

In Alloy, Sam Branden approaches the city as a structure in constant tension pulled apart, stitched together, and continuously reconfigured.Rather than a resolved mixture, alloy becomes a condition where rigidity and elasticity, industrial force and fragility, order and instability coexist.

Branden’s practice does not begin in the studio, but on the street.He has spent years collecting torn, layered, and discarded posters from the urban environment, bringing these ephemeral fragments back into the studio as the basis for ongoing material experimentation.

These materials are not simply incorporated, but stretched, stitched, and reassembled pushed toward a state between control and instability. For Branden, making is a process of testing limits, allowing traces of the city and residues of time to actively shape the work rather than be refined or erased.

The works combine hand-sewn burlap, mesh, spandex, nylon thread, polymer, and found street posters.Materials collide and depend on one another, forming structures that feel precise yet perpetually unsettled.

Color plays a vital role throughout Alloy. Vibrant clashes, abrupt transitions, and layered mesh introduce rhythm and interruption, echoing the density, noise, and constant flux of urban life.

Fabrics strain against their frames, surfaces remain taut yet unstable. Within this tension, Branden points to a defining condition of contemporary city living between control and escape, structure and collapse.

📍 Pegasus at Love’s Club, Brooklyn
🗓 Oct 24 – Dec 21, 2025
Presented by CHART

Sam Branden 將城市視為一個不斷被拉扯、縫合與重組的結構體。Alloy（合金）不是混合後的穩定狀態，而是一種持續處於張力之中的存在，剛與柔、工業與彈性、秩序與失序同時並存。

Branden 的創作並非始於工作室，而是從街頭開始。他長期在城市中收集被撕裂、覆蓋、遺棄的海報與材料，將這些原本短暫存在於城市視野中的視覺碎片，帶回工作室進行反覆的材料實驗。

這些材料不只是被使用，而是被拉伸、縫合、重新組裝，進入一種介於控制與失控之間的狀態。對 Branden 而言，創作是一個不斷測試材料極限的過程，讓城市的痕跡與時間的殘留，直接參與作品的生成，而非被美化或抹除。

他的作品由手縫粗麻布、網紗、彈性纖維、尼龍線、聚合物與街頭海報共同構成。材料彼此堆疊、對抗，也彼此依存，形成一種不穩定卻精確的結構關係。

色彩在《Alloy》中扮演關鍵角色。高飽和色塊、突兀的轉換、交錯的網狀層次，創造出節奏與中斷，回應城市生活的密度、雜訊與持續變動的能量。

布料緊繃、幾乎溢出畫框；表面看似穩定，卻始終處於臨界狀態。
在這種張力之中，Branden 指向當代城市生活的核心狀態，介於控制與逃逸之間，介於結構與崩解之間。

latestPosts.caption:
🎄 Back at @bairesgrill for the holidays and I’m in HEAVEN! 😍 Manhattan’s hottest Argentinian spot (fresh from their legendary Miami location since ‘99) is giving MAJOR festive vibes just steps from Broadway! ✨

Let’s talk about these EMPANADAS because I could literally eat these ALL DAY! 🥟 Whether you go grilled or fried, and pick beef, chicken, ham & cheese, onion & cheese, or corn - each one is SO authentic, hearty, and absolutely delicious! That first bite hits different every time! 💯

The MILA BEEF NAPOLITANA is giving Italian-Argentinian fusion vibes! 🇦🇷🇮🇹 This crispy, golden fried classic with marinara, ham, and that melty mozzarella-parmesan combo plus fresh tomatoes? Pure comfort on a plate! Comes with your choice of fries, salad, or mashed potatoes!

Feeling fancy? That CONFIT AND GRILLED OCTOPUS is STUNNING! 🐙 Perfectly tender with smashed potatoes and that romesco sauce bringing all the flavors together! Chef’s kiss! 💋

The PASTEL DE PAPA is classic Argentinian comfort! That potato and ground beef pie situation is everything cozy about the holidays! 🥔

Now... the PARRILLADA is what DREAMS are made of! 🥩🔥 We’re talking super tender, juicy skirt steak, flap meat, short ribs, chicken, and here’s the real star: those sweetbreads are TO.DIE.FOR! 😭 Plus sausage and blood sausage all kissed by the grill! But wait... THE.REAL.CHIMICHURRI.SAUCE takes this platter to another UNIVERSE! Your choice of two sides makes this feast complete! #MeatLoversParadise

Finished with an Affogato al Cafe because espresso over vanilla ice cream is always the move! ☕🍨

The warm hospitality, sophisticated yet cozy atmosphere, and bold authentic flavors make this THE spot for holiday celebrations and special events! 🎉

Our City Center offices will close tomorrow, June 20, in observation of Juneteenth.

Juneteenth commemorates the emancipation of the last enslaved people in Southern states that formed the Confederacy during the American Civil War; while the Emancipation Proclamation was issued on January 1, 1863, its purpose was not enacted in many Confederate States until the Union forces arrived. On June 19, 1865, a group of Union soldiers arriving in Galveston, Texas shared the proclamation with Black Americans enslaved there.

As we celebrate Juneteenth, we hope the lessons we learn and the peace we find in observation extends well beyond the holiday into all of our practices as artists and people. Revisit our conversation with Brandon, Kayla, Noax, and Sis, presented in partnership with Broadway for Racial Justice, and join us in renewing our commitment to supporting Black art in all of its joys, victories, and celebrations.
Composer Jason Robert Brown (our upcoming Annual Gala Presentation of PARADE) reflects on Stephen Sondheim's profound influence on Broadway musical theater. #PBSForTheArts
Discover dance at New York City Center, starting this September with Fall for Dance, Twyla Tharp, and more.

It’s Tony Awards Week! The original Broadway production of PARADE received NINE (!!!) @thetonyawards nominations, winning Best Book and Best Original Score! 

Composer and lyricist Jason Robert Brown is nominated again for Best Original Score at this year's ceremony for his work on @mrsatnightbway. Will you be tuning in? 

Don’t forget tickets to City Center’s Annual Gala Presentation of PARADE go on sale to the general public this Tuesday!

“It’s not been easy to be a dancer who’s used her voice so loudly, and it hasn’t come without its reprisal in a sense. But that doesn’t mean that I’m going to stop. None of this work has been for my own advancement. This is for a bigger picture, this is for younger generations."

Georgina Pazcoguin, the self-proclaimed "Rogue Ballerina," is New York City Ballet’s first Asian American woman to be promoted to soloist. As co-founder of Final Bow for Yellowface, an organization she co-founded with Phil Chan in 2017, she has advocated tirelessly to combat the invisibility of Asian American dancers and increase AAPI diversity onstage. Final Bow for Yellowface has asked all ballet companies to commit to hiring an Asian choreographer by 2025 to avoid stereotyped interpretations of stories set in Asian locations.

Georgina most recently performed at City Center in "Sweet Gwen Suite" as part of our 2021 Fall for Dance Festival. Join us today for a TAKEOVER!

On December 11, 1943, we celebrated our very first opening night. ♥️ Happy 82 years to this beautiful institution that belongs to all of us. 

Mayor Fiorello La Guardia designated City Center as Manhattan’s first performing arts center with the mission of making the best in theater, dance, and music accessible to all audiences. 

This commitment continues today, as we serve our audience through school programs, student matinees, masterclasses, and accessible ticketing initiatives. This work has reached over 15,000 participants and continues to grow each season. 

As the year comes to a close, please consider giving a gift of any size today and make your impact beyond the stage count. NYCityCenter.org/Donate

I invested $2,000 of my savings (huge part 😅)and it grew little by little everyday.  Not everyday was glorious, but I have met some amazing people who truly wanted to support me and be part of this journey.  I enjoyed it and was grateful because it taught me so much lesson.
Popup was fun but opening and operating a restaurant on a daily basis is a whole another level.  To be honest, I didn’t even have the 2nd month rent after I paid the 1st one and deposit.  I must be not so rational 😂 but I would never know what I can do until I do it and actually I don’t have much to lose.  At my every popup, I saw the same faces, you guys gave me a huge confidence to feel good to jump off the cliff. 
 I appreciate so many of you who supported from my basement kitchen taking a bus on a stormy day, having KJUN as part of your life, and spending sleepless nights for brainstorming.  It will be forever somewhere in my heart and make me want to be even better. 
 
📸 @danahn17

It’s been crazy but today I finally opened the actual paper of @nytimes and saw myself and @KJUNnyc 🤯 

Coming to New York from Seoul in 2009 was the best and hardest thing that I did.  I was broke and did not know anyone.  But since then, I never stopped!  When I started KJUN at my apartment alone during the pandemic, I was also broke but lucky enough to have wonderful people who supported me. 

I appreciate everyone who has been supportive and was before.  It kept me going when I wanted to give up. 

KJUN is the tiny mini restaurant that I afforded and earned by myself and has been growing everyday.  I am proud of everything about it and not gonna apologize for the size. (So if you are not happy about how small it is, go ahead and write on @yelp 🤪)

latestPosts.caption:
As a professional chef at several fine dining restaurants in NYC for a decade, this name @pete_wells sometimes gave me kitchen nightmares or nerve wracking moments.  I thought (and hoped) it would take at least a year to get @nytimes review or more because I’m still putting a small piece by piece everyday.  When he visited @kjunnyc , I thought he was just a guy in the neighborhood and soon to be my regular. 

My minivan journey started from my tiniest apartment. Later, I got a little fancy and found a few basement kitchens. So many movings and closings.  But mostly this is something that I started with my own money, which was $2,000 and still this is my own restaurant and I am proud of this minivan because I afforded all by myself. 

Where there is a good restaurant, there is a good support. My cooks refused to get a raise, sometimes they tried to return their paycheck to support me to have a restaurant. And your support kept me going nonstop whenever I felt like giving up.  KJUN storefront would not exist without @danahn17 @yondu.usa @theflavorbible nmittel @vic32010 @jj_jeanjo @theboroughbred @clickclickw00t @hoyunah @georgetteny @gpfood

latestPosts.caption: Cooking was my whole life for many years.  I still cooked at home after cooking for 13-14 hours at work.  If I was not cooking at work, I traveled the country and cooked.  Nashville, Austin, Miami, Chicago, New York, Birmingham and Boston…  I went anywhere if there was a chance to cook my own menu and each event was unique.  Sometimes, I had to cook at a garage or in the dark with candles(@wutangchan504 knows it all). I was featured on the cover in NYT, CBS news, Bon Appetit and Food & Wine.  I was broke but happy.  It all felt like magic and I was living my dreams…

latestPosts.caption: I started my career as a chef @restaurantaugustneworleans.  My first week there was the most intense thing I had ever experienced.  I was very foreign — everyone seemed much taller and stronger than I was!  No one spoke English the way I learned it, so I was always confused.  Learning to cook was one thing, but learning it in a new language seemed impossible.  My first mentor, Chef @michaelgulotta taught me all the fundamentals with patience and showed me a great example.  I was lucky to work for him.  Learning all the stations including private dining, off-site events and butchery at Restaurant August helped me build a foundation for my career.  For the first time, I saw my name on the menu next to dishes I created.  I worked about 14 hours a day instead of hanging out at the bars I came home so excited to write more recipes and ideas…

latestPosts.caption: After my externship in New Orleans in 2010, I returned to @theculinaryinstituteofamerica.  My time at the school gave me a strong foundation to start working at any restaurant.  Learning wines and restaurant laws was fun, but I missed NOLA and knew that I wanted to move back after graduation.  I was ready and excited to get into the real cook’s life…

latestPosts.caption: When I was leaving Korea for New York, my friend said “If you go to America, you must go to New Orleans”. I did not know that would change my life.  All I knew was Hurricane Katrina.  I remember that I was sitting in couch at home in Korea when I watched the news on the Hurricane wondering where it exactly was in the world.  My dad loves music and told me about Louis Armstrong sometimes.  In 2009, when I was @theculinaryinstituteofamerica , I decided to do my externship in NOLA for 4 months.  Saints won the Superbowl then it was Mardi Gras!  I felt like the city was welcoming me and I was meant to be there ❤️ To be continued…
latestPosts.alt: Photo by JAE JUNG (정재은) in New Orleans, Louisiana with @kjunnyc. May be pop art of tambourine and text.

latestPosts.caption: On February the first in 2009, I left Korea for New York to go to @theculinaryinstituteofamerica.  I was excited about the new adventure but also nervous.  I remember that I cried the whole time during the 3 connecting flights.  I was broke and my parents did not love my choice.  I had small savings and had to make it last as long as possible.  I couldn’t imagine what it would be like to learn something new in a new language in a new country.  After landing at JFK, everything was overwhelming.  It was definitely not what I saw in the SEX AND THE CITY!  But I knew that was the best thing I did for myself and I would be just fine because I believed in myself!  To be continued…

NYC’S HOTTEST LATIN LOVE STORY 🔥💕
Just experienced ❤️Friday Nightand I’m OBSESSED! 

📍 CHICA & THE DON @chicaandthedon 
📍 24 E 21st St New York, NY 10010

This isn’t just dinner, it’s a whole VIBE! Born from a real love story, you can literally FEEL the passion in every corner 💫 The energy hits different - sophisticated yet vibrant, like stepping into the most romantic telenovela 🌹

Started with THE DON cocktail - toki whiskey with mamajuana and tamarind? GENIUS! 🥃 Then tried CHICA with coconut and strawberry condensed milk - basically vacation in a glass 🏝️ The Espresso “Chery” Martini was the perfect nightcap - Grey Goose meets Licor 43 perfection ☕️✨

Food game is UNREAL! 🔥 That Tuna Taco with gochujang sesame mayo had me questioning everything I thought I knew about tacos 🌮 The Blue Crab Tostada was Instagram gold - manchego mornay with grilled corn? Chef’s kiss 🦀

But the BIRRIA EMPANADAS stole my heart! Braised short rib with Oaxaca cheese and that consomé for dipping - I’m literally drooling thinking about it 🤤 Ended with the Oxtail Saltado and those crispy fries mixed with tender braised oxtail? ICONIC 🍟

The night vibes are EVERYTHING - dim lighting, Latin beats, and that romantic energy that makes every moment feel cinematic 🎬 Perfect for date night or celebrating with your crew!

latestPosts.caption:
One Of A Kind Luxury Glamping Retreat🌅🏕️

@collectiveretreats feels worlds away from the city, yet you can still see the skyline twinkling across the harbor. 
I recently stayed in their Summit Suite, and honestly, it’s one of the most peaceful stays I’ve ever experienced in New York.

🏕️ This suite brings modern comfort to the outdoors.
Every detail is crafted for comfort, from a complimentary in-room Trail Bar stocked with a variety of cold beverages plus a French press and kettle for brewing your own morning coffee or tea.

☕️ You can sip it on your terrace as the city slowly comes alive in the distance.
Inside, you’ll find plush bedding, climate control, blackout drapes, and Wi-Fi, so it’s just as relaxing indoors as it is outside. And the best part? 

🌙Each stay includes nightly turn-down treats and your own personal fire pit to enjoy under the stars. 

When you’re ready to explore Governors Island, you can take a scenic bike around the island or head to Three Peaks Lodge, that’s their on-site restaurant.
Every meal feels like it was designed to be savored slowly with views of the harbor and Statue of Liberty in the distance.

If you’re searching for a luxury getaway that blends nature, design, and a touch of magic  Collective Governors Island is it. 
It’s truly peaceful escape, right in the heart of New York City. 🗽

🏕️ LOCATION: Collective Retreats – Governors Island 📍 DISTANCE: 8-minute ferry from Lower Manhattan ⏰ SEASONAL OPENING:  May–October 🥂 WHERE TO DINE: Three Peaks Lodge 🚲TO NOTE: The island is Car-free

Hey friends 🌿

Starting November 11, Lula will now be open:

Tuesday–Saturday
Closed Sunday & Monday

The restaurant world asks a lot of people. Creating a great meal and genuine hospitality night after night takes focus, energy, and care. Burnout is real — and balance matters. When life feels grounded, the work follows.

I think being vulnerable in this industry isn’t always commonplace — which is a shame. Our guests are part of who we are, and we owe it to you to be real and authentic about what it takes to do what we love every day.

This small schedule change helps our team keep that balance so we can continue to show up with the same energy and spirit that make Lula what it is.

Sometimes people like to call restaurants the land of misfit toys. There’s some truth in that — we’re a mix of personalities and stories — but we also know exactly how we fit: to feed people, to take care of others, and to be part of something bigger than ourselves.

Please come join us for our first TUESDAY service on November 11. We can’t wait to welcome you. Resy link in the bio 🔗 

We’re always here for your celebrations, get-togethers, hangouts, and more — reach out anytime about private dining or special events.

— Conor

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Trace links between the Frick's predominantly European collection and the wider world. In this episode of "Where in the World?," Curator Aimee Ng dives deep into the history of pearls and their appearance in paintings by Vermeer.

In the seventeenth century, the expensive natural gems made their way to Holland from Dutch colonies along the Indian Ocean, where skilled divers harvested them under dangerous conditions.

Explore the full series at the link in bio.

Happy #WomensEqualityDay from The Frick Collection! We are celebrating by reminiscing on our 2020 series, “What’s Her Story?”

The year 2020 commemorated the one-hundredth anniversary of women’s right to vote across the United States. The Frick celebrated with a series of videos honoring the stories of women at the museum who made, appeared in, collected, and took care of art in this collection.

In the first episode of the series, Curator Aimee Ng considers a portrait of Louise de Broglie, Comtesse d’Haussonville. Explore the full series at the link in bio.

Look to the skies! ☀ In time for tomorrow's #summersolstice, gaze at a new list of recommended reads from the #FrickLibrary all about astronomy in art.

Celebrate the official first day of the season by exploring publications on the Big Bang and Renaissance astrology, and discover one of the oldest books in the library's collections. Find the full list at the link in our bio.
—
Astronomy Reading List books in front of François Boucher's "Four Seasons: Summer" (1755) at Frick Madison. Producer: George Koelle

Happy Jewish American Heritage Month! ✡ In celebration, the #FrickLibrary offers a recommended reading list of books highlighting the contributions of Jewish American artists, scholars, and collectors.

At the link in our bio, learn about ten titles ranging from monographs on artists like Mark Rothko and Helen Frankenthaler to bilingual books in Yiddish and Spanish and explorations of the sacred and secular.

The Frick presents Cheng-Harrell Open Nights, a new seasonal series of free public evenings held at Frick Madison! The series kicks off on June 17 with a Pride Month celebration inspired by our installation series "Living Histories: Queer Views and Old Masters." 

From 5:00 to 9:00 p.m., the event will include gallery talks, sketching, live music, and after-hours access to the museum and reading room. Plus, a special panel discussion moderated by Xavier F. Salomon, Deputy Director and Peter Jay Sharp Chief Curator, will feature writer and cultural critic Roxane Gay (@roxanegay74) along with "Living Histories" artists Jenna Gribbon (@jennagribbon), Doron Langberg (@doronlangberg), and Salman Toor (@salman.toor). 

The panel will also be livestreamed with CART captioning, and ASL interpretation will be provided in person for the gallery talks and panel discussion.

CLOSING SOON—Jenna Gribbon's (@jennagribbon) "What Am I Doing Here? I Should Ask You the Same" is on view at #FrickMadison through May 22. Her painting is the third installation in our ongoing series "Living Histories: Queer Views and Old Masters."

Jenna sat down with Xavier F. Salomon, Deputy Director and Peter Jay Sharp Chief Curator, to discuss her inspirations and shared why she thinks Fragonard's Progress of Love panels would be the most fun works of art at the Frick to recreate. 📺 

Watch the full interview on our YouTube channel (link in bio).

The Frick Collection asked each "Living Histories" artist to present a work in response to paintings in the permanent collection.

Jenna Gribbon (@jennagribbon) chose to create a work that would counter the Frick's traditional displays of husbands, wives, and male rivalry. Her painting “What Am I Doing Here? I Should Ask You the Same,” a powerful portrait of her partner created in response to the work of Hans Holbein, is on view now through May 22 as part of "Living Histories: Queer Views and Old Masters."

📺 Watch the full conversation at the link in our bio.

Stop scrolling, start strolling.

Frick fans far and wide can roam the galleries of our temporary home, #FrickMadison, at frick.org/virtualtour (link in bio). Discover highlights from the permanent collection like Fragonard's Progress of Love—displayed beyond the walls of the Frick mansion for the first time in over 100 years.

Cheers to one year!

#FrickMadison opened to the public one year ago today. During the move from The Frick Collection’s historic buildings, iconic works of art embarked on a journey to their temporary new home five blocks away. In this never-before-seen video, enjoy a look at the Frick’s exceptional team of art handlers as they reinstall a familiar face from the collection.

🆓🎟️ As a thank-you for your enthusiasm and support this past year, we're giving away a pair of FREE TICKETS to TEN FOLLOWERS! In the comments, let us know why you love the Frick and tag your +1 to Frick Madison. We'll randomly select ten lucky commenters.
—
#Rembrandt's Polish Rider (ca. 1655) being moved to Frick Madison. Produced by George Koelle

Have you visited Jenna Gribbon's (@jennagribbon) work yet at #FrickMadison?

📺 The artist sat down with Xavier F. Salomon, Deputy Director and Peter Jay Sharp Chief Curator, to discuss engaging critically with the history of art and enlivening the Old Masters through the lens of the camp aesthetic. Watch the full conversation at the link in bio.

🎨 Gribbon's painting, "What Am I Doing Here? I Should Ask You the Same," is on view as part of "Living Histories: Queer Views and Old Masters" through May 22.

latestPosts.caption:
To commemorate Christmas Eve, we’re taking a close look at “The Annunciation” by Italian Renaissance artist Fra Filippo Lippi 👼

A Carmelite priest and a teacher to artists such as Botticelli, Lippi on numerous occasions depicted the Annunciation, a popular subject in mid-fifteenth-century Florence. The Biblical scene tells the story of the angel Gabriel visiting the Virgin Mary to tell her that she will give birth to the son of God. The artist usually placed the figures in elegant and complex architectural settings, rife with symbolic objects and flowering plants. Here, however, he depicts a simple, bare background, with nothing to distract the viewer from the quiet drama at play.

🕊️ The lily carried by Gabriel symbolizes the Virgin’s purity, while the dove represents his words to her: “The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee.”
—
Fra Filippo Lippi (Italian, ca. 1406–1469), The Annunciation, ca. 1440. Tempera on poplar panel, left panel: 25 1/8 x 9 7/8 in. (63.8 x 25.1 cm), right panel: 25 1/8 x 10 in. (63.8 x 25.4 cm). The Frick Collection, New York

latestPosts.caption:
To round out our 90th-anniversary week, we’re partnering with our sister institution @FrickPittsburgh to commemorate the birth of museum founder Henry Clay Frick, #bornonthisday in 1849 🎂
 
A coke and steel industrialist, Frick became known for his business acumen and ruthless labor practices. After establishing himself in the coke industry, he and his wife, Adelaide Howard Childs, moved to Pittsburgh and purchased Clayton, the home where they would live for nearly two decades—today part of The Frick Pittsburgh.
 
It was around this time that Frick began developing his art collection. He would continue collecting until he died in 1919, in the New York City mansion he commissioned to house his art. In his will, he left the building and its contents to become a museum “for the use and benefit of all persons whomsoever.”

Today, The Frick Collection in New York and The Frick Pittsburgh remain important cultural sites, showcasing the Fricks’ family homes and collections and providing invaluable historical insight into the Gilded Age.

Curious to learn more about early Frick history? Visit frick.org/about or discover our full suite of publications on the family at frick.org/shop.
—

Almost 3 years ago, my husband found this location on Facebook Marketplace (yes you read that correctly lol). After seeing so many spaces, the moment I stepped into this one I had a gut feeling. It was intimate, big and small in all the right ways, and somehow I knew it was meant for us. 
We started this journey not knowing much, and in these last two years of being open the growth has been substantial. The highs have been incredibly high, and the lows have been very low, testing everything I know about myself as a leader, a mother, and a wife. But no matter what, I always come back to that little voice in my head telling me to weather the storm.
I believe in my brand. I believe my community loves what we create. And from day one, pouring back into this business has been our thing. 
Redoing our space isn’t just a blessing it’s something we’ve worked relentlessly for. I am blessed, I am fortunate, and somehow we always find a way. And now, I cannot wait for you to see the revelation of our renewed space 🌴🥂🌱🦋

I don’t have words really just a lot of feelings. Today is my mom’s birthday. What would have been her 75th birthday. Wow I miss this Woman! HAAM exists becuase of HER! Healthy as a motha was born becuase of HER! I am who I am because of HER! I miss her so much! Help me wish mi mami a happy heavenly birthday 🕊️💙🦋

latestPosts.caption:
“When I say I want to fall in love offline, this is what I mean…

Not through swipes, disappearing messages, or algorithms telling me who I should fancy. But through the real stuff, locking eyes across a crowded room, bumping into someone at a bookshop event, or laughing with a stranger over a glass of wine until it doesn’t feel like you’re strangers anymore.

Falling in love offline is about allowing those raw, human moments to happen. The ones that are a little clumsy, a little unexpected, and a lot more magical because they weren’t manufactured by a screen.

This is what we’ve been building with BODA - spaces where you can show up as yourself, meet people who are also looking for something real, and rediscover the joy of connection without the pressure of ‘performing’ online.

Because romance isn’t dead. It just got buried under apps, and we’re here to dig it out again. 💌”

Ciao ragazzi! Meet Nick. Many of you may know him as the one and only #Cannoliguy, owner and operator of @carrellodicannoli . Nick has been perfecting his mobile cannoli business for the past five years. He has brought a little taste of Sicily to each event that he has been blessed to be a part of. 

While Nick continues to work private events with his team of #Cannoliguys, God has opened another door, allowing him to embark on a new journey. 

@thecannolishopnj will soon open its doors, allowing each guest to experience the authentic taste of our custom cannoli. Guests will be able to choose between 15 different toppings, specialty drizzles and so much more. Pair that with a fresh cup of our espresso based beverages, and you will be transported to Italy in no time. 

We thank you for being here & supporting our journey. Look out for upcoming announcements and opening dates. We can’t wait for you to stop by! 🇮🇹❤️🙏🏻

‘Somm Sips’ debuts with a showstopper: Château Lafite Rothschild 1989. A “dark horse” standout vintage of the eighties and one of the greatest Bordeaux vintages of the century, this bottle hits that perfect “Goldilocks” stride. 
 
Initially beginning with challenging conditions that emerge triumphantly in the glass, it’s a testament to Lafite’s unwavering craftsmanship and dedication to exceptional quality, no matter the conditions. 

Lafite embodies everything we love in a wine, and pairs best with our Ribeye of Beef or Dry-Aged Duck. 
 
Stay tuned as Somm Sips continues, exploring our sommelier’s top picks, rare vintages, and hidden gems.

latestIgtvVideos.title: Chipotle-Orange Pulled Pork Recipe
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Back with another recipe that you can cook at home with your kids, Chef Doherty and Emmet are making a fall-off-the-bone pulled pork that is loaded with flavor.

Method:
Pre heat oven to 325 degrees F
Combine all Spice rub ingredients in a bowl. Score the skin on pork shoulder and create several deep holes with a knife. Rub spice blend deep into holes and rub the remainder over the surface and season with salt. Using a roasting pan, cook for 3 hours uncovered at 325F. Then, lower the temp to 300F, add 1 cup of water and cook for two more hours. Remove from oven and skim the fat from the surface of the pan juices. Use two forks to pull meat apart and add pan juice back to the pulled meat. You are now ready to eat this any way you want!

Ingredients:
One 6-8 Lb. Pork Shoulder

Spice Rub
5 Cloves of Garlic, minced
Zest of ½ orange
5 tsp Smoked Paprika
4 tsp Sweet Paprika
1 tsp Ground Chipotle Pepper
½ tsp Cayenne Pepper
1 ½ tsp ground Cumin
3 tsp Ground Coriander
2 Tbs Light Brown Sugar
2Tbsp Cocoa Powder
3 Tbs Vegetable Oil
Salt 
Serves 8-10

latestIgtvVideos.title: Black Bean Country Style Soup Recipe with Chef Doherty & Emmett
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Cooking with your kids at home can be a lot of fun. Chef Doherty and his son Emmett are back with a Black Bean Soup recipe that’s easy to make and tastes amazing!

Method:
In a quart-size pot over medium heat, and cook the bacon until it browns. Remove from pot and set aside. Cook the onions, celery and leeks in the bacon fat until they are tender. 
Add carrots and garlic and cook a few minutes longer. Add the spices, black beans, chicken stock, salt and the cooked bacon.

Bring to a boil and cook at a slow simmer until the beans are tender.  Soup should be hearty, but if it is too thick add more stock or water. Then add lime juice and garnish with cilantro.

Ingredients:

1/3 cup bacon, diced
2/3 cup onion, diced
2/3 cup celery, diced
1/3 cup leeks, diced
1 cup carrots, diced
3 cloves garlic, ground
1 tsp. cumin, ground
3 tsp. coriander, ground
Cayenne pepper to taste

3/4 lb. black beans, soaked overnight
48 oz chicken stock
3 tsp. salt
2 T. lime juice
Cilantro leaves for garnish

latestPosts.caption: I counted, and I have over 15 photos of the @thaidiner sausage egg sandwich *alone* on my phone. It’s always the same gooey, crispy, affordable plate of perfect, and that’s kind of the best part. So much about the last 5 years has been about change and adapting to chaos, but I’m grateful to have this one corner on Mott and Kenmare when I’m craving a little stability. Also grateful that there are still opportunities to publish odes and essays and the kinds of food writing actual people (not just the algorithm or advertisers) want to read, so thank you @resy @deannating ✨ link in bio/stories!

latestPosts.caption:
Did you know there’s an underground, cavelike restaurant and lounge in the Lower East Side that’s been here for over 20 years?! We checked it out last weekend and it was so cool! 

This is @lacavernanyc, and they serve Tex-Mex food that is SO good and also SO reasonably priced, plus great drinks AND they have live music performances all the time. The tacos and the House Churrasco were delicious, and they also do a Bottomless Margarita Dinner as well which is DEFINITELY worth checking out. 

All in all, @lacavernanyc is a 10 out of 10 and if you haven’t been there yet, add it to your bucket list - ASAP.

latestPosts.caption:
✨Today was one of those amazing days.✨

🥂I had three full beautiful conversations that amounted to a total of six hours of engagement.🥂

1️⃣I started the day with a conversation with @illinois1867 to potentially be involved in a future study related speech and cerebral palsy. 

2️⃣I then had a long thorough discussion with a director studying at the Shakespeare Institute in the United Kingdom. We discussed ACCESS, DISABILITY, and DEAF CULTURE. The focus was on the different access between @actorsequity and @equityuk. Our conversation diverged and expanded into many topics and focused on many issues.

3️⃣I then had an engaging meal with editor of one of the main Broadway and Theatre Outlets. Our conversation focused on on ACCESS, competing ACCESS NEEDS, and future goals. It was a long awaited goal to connect with this theatre personality. And it hits different when someone like that looks you plainly in the face and says, “You will. You will be the first stage manager on Broadway with Cerebral Palsy.” @broadwaycom 

4️⃣I then spent the final hours of the afternoon with Donja. Donja has been in my circle since the pandemic. It has been an honor get to know them beyond managing the ANNUAL WRITE IT OUT program, which celebrates its fifth year this December. This program is something special for me. Both professional and personally. This conversation,and most of my conversations with Donja go DEEP. @bcefa 

🧚🏼‍♂️I  finish the day reflecting on how much I have grown since my first professional gigs in 2005, the relationships I have built over the years, and the influence I have.🦋

💚I hope I’ve made you proud . IUKUK.💜

For intimate yet charming and quirky atmospheres, visit Pocket Bar 57, Pocket Bar NYC, or Back Pocket. I had the privilege of sketching all three of their locations in Manhattan.

Pocket Bar has been the recipient of the “Love Your Local” grant, awarded to the 20 best small businesses in all five boroughs by the mayor of NYC. In addition, it was also the winner of W42ST’s Best Bar 2022-23, an accolade highlighting its beloved status in the Hell's Kitchen community and it's commitment to welcoming all patrons.

Adding to their achievements, they received their own wine label from notable winemaker Bruce Schneider and opened a second location, Back Pocket Bar, all within their first five years of business. The combination of unique wines and cozy, eclectic decor has made Pocket Bar a standout destination!

INCREDIBLE BYOB NJ STEAKHOUSE

Charkol in Freehold, NJ is one of my favorite BYOB NJ steakhouses. And for good reason! They have amazing appetizers like the whipped ricotta and pizza with burratta and hot honey. You have to go for their dry aged steaks as well. For sides try the brussel sprouts, lobster mac n cheese and creamed mushrooms. And for dessert the bread pudding is my FAV!!! I seriously love this NJ restaurant and frequent it often. They also have incredible service. Shoutout to the best waiter, Leif! Check out @thecharkol

INCREDIBLE BYOB NJ STEAKHOUSE 🥩 

Finally tried Charkol in Freehold, NJ this weekend and it was incredible! From the appetizers, to their amazing steaks and desserts this meal did not disappoint. Definitely add this NJ steakhouse to your list. Highly recommend their wood fired pizza - I know we have great NJ pizza and this was up there. The clams and the pork belly were insane. I absolutely loved their dry-aged porterhouse for 2. Perfectly cooked with a side of their signature steak sauce, bone marrow and chimichurri. For sides get the lobster mac n cheese and brussel sprouts. And OF COURSE get all the desserts ❤️

I was so impressed with the service, the ambiance and the quality of food. This is a must try NJ restaurant and I will definitely be back. Love that it’s BYOB and you can check out their NJ brewery next door @artisbrewery 🍻 absolutely loved our experience at @thecharkol

latestPosts.caption:
NYC’s food halls and markets can be pricey, but there’s a hidden gem lunch special in Time Out Market Union Square.

For $15 at Fornino’s Time Out Union Square location, you get an entire pizza and small salad. For your pizza, choose a margherita or the market special (which is a chef choice specialty pizza). The side salads can be a caesar, gem, kale or green market (another chef special).

This style of pizza is usually not my top choice, but this was my first time trying Fornino and I was very impressed. It had a great char and lots of flavor, probably from all the olive oil Michael topped it with!

You can find this deal at Time Out Market Union Square, which is located at 121 E 14th St.

follow @tayloreatsnyc for more NYC food deals & restaurant recs!

Ease into the season with our new pours, made for cozy tables and long nights:
• Fornino Spritz — cappelletti aperitivo blend with prosecco. 
• The Bitter Spagliato — cocchi vermouth di torino, cinzano rosso, prosecco. 
• Pera Verde — pear, rosemary, ginger, martini & rossi extra dry, cocchi americano. 

The perfect first sip before pizza, wine, and celebration.

Celebrate the season this New Years Eve with The Feast of Seven Fishes @theottersoho 

This Intimate, Coastal-Inspired Feast begins with a Sicilian Crudo of Tuna, Salmon, and Scallops, followed by Octopus with Capers and Parsley Root. Housemade Sea Urchin Spaghetti anchors a silky Shrimp Scampi, paving the way for a delicate Black Cod Bourride.

The evening concludes with a playful finale: Taiyaki served with Pistachio and Coffee–Saffron Ice Cream.

Each course is elevated by thoughtfully curated wine pairings, designed to complement the menu’s bright, briny, and expressive flavors. Enjoy a Champagne toast & bottle selections to continue the celebration.

We’re beginning 2026 with a celebration close to home. From January 7-26, join us for 20 days of Chef Daniel Humm’s 20-Year Retrospective, Presented by @Resy.

Honoring @danielhumm’s twentieth anniversary as the Chef of Eleven Madison Park, this limited-time menu revisits defining moments in our story — from the early “Grid Menu” era to “I Love New York” and the chapters that have followed. Each course reflects a dish, an idea, or a turning point that has shaped both Chef Humm’s journey and the evolution of Eleven Madison Park.

Join us as we celebrate two decades of creativity and transformation. Reservations available now through the @Resy app.

latestPosts.caption:
The Celery Root dish from 2014 is one we’re especially excited to revisit for Chef @danielhumm’s 20-Year Retrospective, presented by @Resy.

Inspired by the French technique of cooking a chicken en vessie, or in a bladder, Chef Humm reimagined the approach using a humble vegetable.

Both simple and defining, the Celery Root became the inspiration for our four Kitchen Fundamentals, which continue to shape how we develop dishes today.

Join us for this retrospective menu from January 7-26, 2026. Reserve your seat through the @Resy app or via the link in our bio.

Treat them to drinks at our bar or a full tasting menu — e-gift cards are available on our website and make the perfect last-minute present.⁠

We have several witches hanging out on our patio today! Come down to eat some delicious food and take some fun photos!
Our pasta fagioli is good for the soul. Come and try it today!!!
Fun with fundraising!
Happy birthday to Brianna!

Pete Ippolito opened Pietro's in 1976 with his gimmick (as he would refer to the idea) of offering a sesame seed edge pizza.  In fact, he was the first to use sesame seeds on the edge of a pizza and tried to trademark his concept in the 1970’s but it was turned down as food recipes itself do not qualify. 
 
The original offering of sesame seeds came with an extra fee but for the extra few cents, no one would bite.  He then switched up his idea and offered it for free on all pizzas and the rest is history!  46 years later, 8 out of 10 pizzas sold at Pietro’s are made with sesame, garlic- seed, garlic, onion, salt, poppy or everything crust! 
 
We even do it on all of our calzones and rolls as well as they are all made to order!

Our logo since 1976 has always been the red and white “canopy” which symbolizes the entryway to the restaurant. We decided to take that little piece of history and carry it into our outdoor space but with a bit of a different spin! Check this out….#umbrellaskyproyect
This weather calls for some homemade pasta fagioli!

Tonight was pure magic ✨

Every single seat was filled. Inside. Outside. Every table buzzing. And then, out of nowhere, the Fire Department walked in with Frosty and Santa 🎅🏻☃️🚒

The entire dining room lit up instantly. We just happened to have so many kids dining with us, and every single one of them got a fire hat. Smiles everywhere. Eyes wide. Parents filming. Kids cheering. The vibe was unreal.

I teared up watching it all unfold. This surprise wasn’t random. It was a reminder that when you show up for your community, your community shows up for you. And tonight, they showed up in the most magical way.

So grateful for our local heroes, our incredible guests, and a room full of joy, laughter, and Christmas spirit ❤️🍕🚒

We’ve always known it — but now, it’s official: Italian cuisine is an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity! ✨ This recognition by UNESCO celebrates not just the flavors, but the cultures that have shaped our understanding of food over the centuries.
 
For us, food is culture. It’s a mosaic of knowledge, dialogue, and influences that build bridges between people. This is the profound meaning of Italian cuisine as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity: affirming and sharing the values of intercultural exchange, culinary freedom, and gastronomic diversity.
 
At Eataly, we believe in a cuisine that unites, honors its roots, and is curious about the world. Every day in our stores, we celebrate the quality, the territories, the people, and the knowledge that make Italian cuisine a living, ever-evolving heritage — one to be preserved, passed on, and respectfully enriched.

We know how to celebrate the holiday season ✨🎄

Try all of our new Eataly treats, crafted fresh the Italian way and available in-store at our counters.

latestPosts.caption:
“ GO BIG OR GO HOME “ said by Chef Amita, Executive Chef of @khaosan_nyc 

Born and raised in Udonthani, Thailand, Chef Amita Phookaw discovered her love for cooking at an early age. Growing up with her grandmother—who loved preparing hearty home-cooked meals—Amita spent her childhood helping in the kitchen and learning the secrets of traditional Thai cooking.

By the age of 20, she was already mastering the art of Isaan cuisine, using fresh, homegrown ingredients harvested from her family’s garden. This connection to the land shaped her philosophy: only fresh, clean, and chemical-free ingredients can bring out the true soul of Thai flavors.

In 2017, Amita moved to New York City, where she worked in both Japanese and Thai restaurants, gaining new techniques and broadening her culinary perspective. Combining these experiences with her deep-rooted Thai heritage, she opened Khaosan in 2022.

At Khaosan, Chef Amita stays true to her guiding principle: authentic Thai flavors crafted with the freshest ingredients. Every dish is a celebration of her grandmother’s cooking, her Isaan roots, and her culinary journey—bringing the warmth of Thai home cooking to every plate.

📸 by @buchyyy_buabucha

latestPosts.caption:
Many of you know me as Nelly, but my mother was the only person who consistently called me by my birth name — Nelida. 
When she passed away this September, I felt that silence deeply. And in that silence, I realized something important:
If I no longer have her voice, I can still let the memory of her live through community, creativity, and connection.

She named me Nelida, one of the most Puerto Rican names on the western hemisphere, lol. She was bed bound and immobile for
the latter part of her life. She wasn’t able to be as social, she wasn’t able to connect with people how she once did. She lives on through
me, through my name. Everytime I see my name, I think of the time my mother put into making me the person that I am today.

So I created Nelida paint.sip.connect.
A space where we can step away from life’s obstacles, breathe, laugh, paint, sip, talk, and reconnect with ourselves. The smile you see on me today? It’s because I hear my mother’s voice in every attendee who shows up to experience something beautiful with us.

My hope is simple:
May my sessions feed the soul
May they soothe you, inspire you, and remind you that you are allowed to create, express, and enjoy the beauty that life is.

Our first event took place at Fushimi Times Square, truly a gem in the area. With incredible food, perfect drinks, gorgeous ambience, it was the ideal home for this new chapter.

And yes… we had real Bad Bunny fans in the room — one guest even shared she has attended every BB concert! 🎤🐰
Between raffles, trivia, curated music by The Headliners Inc, and the energy in the room… it was truly unforgettable.

Thank you to everyone who clicked on Eventbrite, saved the date, and showed up for this dream.
From an analog girl who suddenly found herself in the digital world… thank you for helping me honor my mother, my name, and this purpose.

Welcome to Nelida paint.sip.connect.
Where art meets healing, community meets joy, and everyone has a seat at the table.

Thanks to @salviclaudi88 @designitwithvicki @theheadlinersinc @fushiminyc @mediatycoonnyc @antman7788 & Everyone Else who made this event possible.

Peace, Love, and Happy Connections!

NELIDA

a treasure realized over generations, 
and a family, called to a purpose.

This is more than a birthright. 
This is destiny, written in the stars 
Born, from the light of the sun.

This is family.

latestIgtvVideos.caption: There are only 5 more Mingus Mondays with the @mingusbigband performances left at #TheDjango! Don’t miss your chance to experience this Grammy award-winning band on our stage with an early and let set at 7:30PM & 9:30PM every Monday with August 28th being the last!

The demi-disco ball or demilune mirrorball is an early disco ball from the Art deco period 1920s-1940s. Generally to be found in ballrooms to achieve a stardust affect. Later, in the mid-century, they were used in roller discos, and we have one always turning at #TheDjango 🪩
~
🎥 @ittaish

Wednesday 7/6!
@elewrockjazz performing twice!

First Show

Famed pianist, composer and Thelonious Monk Competition winner Eric Lewis leads a dynamic trio for a night of genre-bending jazz you won’t forget!

Second Show:

Piano renegade Eric Lewis seamlessly marries jazz, pop and electronics into a sound all his own. Have you ever seen a pianist work the turntable from his piano bench? You will at the Django! 

Get your Resy now!

April marks the centennial of Charles Mingus’ birth and The Django will be celebrating all things Mingus all month long with not just the Mingus Big Band for our “Mingus Mondays” series but also ten members from this Grammy Award winning band leading their own performances with unique arrangements of the music of Charles Mingus. 

On 4/18 we will even be selling the re-issue of “Mingus Three” out on Rhino Records, and Mingus’ original bass will be played for the entire performance! Check our website for full lineup and showtimes!
The award winning Mingus Big Band returns this Monday (and every Monday) with two sets at 7:30PM & 9:30PM 🎷 Make your Resy now!

Join us for “Mingus Fest” this Holiday weekend, as we feature the Mingus Dynasty tonight from 7:30PM-9:30PM, and the Grammy Award winning Mingus Big Band tomorrow with two show times at 7:30PM and 9:30PM! Tune into the livestream from anywhere at www.charlesmingus.com

latestPosts.caption:
Descend into The Django at The Roxy Hotel and you’ll feel like you’ve entered another world. This subterranean jazz club and restaurant in downtown New York City, with its vaulted ceilings and exposed brick walls, was modeled after the boîtes of Paris. 

Over the past decade, The Django has become a place to call home for musicians and audiences alike, providing opportunities for rising stars, seasoned performers, and eager audiences to enjoy a range of jazz music 7 nights a week. The music is complemented by a hand-crafted cocktail program by award-winning mixologists Natasha David & Jeremy Oertel, along with an elevated dinner menu that's perfect for special occasions. 

When the night comes, The Django jams! #thedjangonyc #MeetMeAtTheRoxy #jazz #nycjazz

latestPosts.caption:
I stopped by @passerinenyc last night to check out their pop-up with @chaatdog, and it was such a good reminder of why pop-ups are fun in the first place.

There’s something exciting about the juxtaposition — Passerine’s thoughtful, seasonal Indian cooking alongside Chaat Dog’s bold, playful chaat energy. Different styles, same table. It creates a new way to experience the space, the food, and the people around you.

Pop-ups like this turn dinner into a shared moment — less about formality, more about discovery, conversation, and enjoying great food in a fresh context. @chefchetanshetty and @pervaizistan thank you! 

📍 @passerinenyc 
🌭 Pop-up runs through 12/20

latestPosts.caption:
The latke, like the hot dog, is a blank canvas for cultural interpretation. 

For more than a decade, myself and a bunch of friends have gathered this time of year to celebrate Hanukkah’s fried potato of choice in some form of latke extravaganza.

The Chaat-ke is one we came up with shortly after Chaat Dog was born — a mashup of latke + chaat!

In creating the menu for the collab with @passerinenyc, @pervaizistan and @chefchetanshetty decided to make it public. Three latkes with a slight pakora flavor each topped with a different chaat: apple, roasted corn & poblano and potato.

Thanks to @tooomuchfoood & @eater_ny for including the Chaat-ke on your latke list this holiday season. It’s not fusion, it’s American food. 

Walk in only. Available daily starting at 5 pm thru Dec. 20 in the Drawing Room and bar at Passerine.

Happy holidays, folks!

Photos @eli.eli.eli.eli.eli & @tooomuchfoood

A well made sour looks simple in the glass, but there is a lot happening in each sip. A few small tips to enjoy it fully:

🔹 Let the foam settle.
Give the cocktail a moment so the froth sets and the texture evens out.
🔹 Smell before you sip.
The citrus and aromatics show up first on the nose, then on the palate.
🔹 Sip through the foam, not around it.
That top layer is there for texture, creaminess against bright acidity.
🔹 Take small, slow sips.
Sours are about balance, not speed. Notice the shift from tart to smooth.
🔹 Pair with something savory.
They are perfect before seafood like crudo, oysters, or anything with a little salinity.

Perfect for a pre-dinner pause at the bar, or the first chapter of your evening at @pointsevennyc

HAPPY NEW YEAR VEGANIZERS!!!

As our first new moon approaches, big January 1st energy comes straight from the words of @sourcemessages

…As you grow, your environment will want to change. Let it! It’s time to move into new energy, new opportunities, new habits. Ones that support the wholeness of who you now are. You asked for big changes and the Universe is ready to provide. But you have be willing to allow the shifts to occur. This is no time to try hold on to anything that’s moving out. This is a season of liberation…

Wishing everyone a very happy, safe, and healthy New Year 🙏🌱💕

Have yourself a very Vegan Christmas 🙏🎄💕

🌙In the true holiday spirit, no matter where you are, who you are with, or what you maybe doing, our hope is you can take a moment to look up at the moon- her reflection always has so much to say. These holidays fall over her waning gibbous phase, and we are reminded of her desire to restore balance and release what doesn’t serve us. Offer it up. And, in the perfect holiday spirit, perhaps we can take a moment to offer up a little extra support and cheer to someone in our life or community. We all need it. With so much love, have a beautiful celebration and day wherever you may be✨

Both locations are open regular hours for all of your vegan needs. 🙏🌱💕

Wishing everyone a very happy and safe holiday!

We are open for regular operating hours over Christmas and New Years and we welcome in-house dining, takeout and delivery. Stay safe everyone have have a beautiful holiday!

This is hands down the prettiest halal restaurants we’ve ever been to. This is the BASKING RIDGE location of Hills of Herat, which was opened earlier last year. They get packed real quick so please make reservations. Lines pile on quick out the door for seating on busy nights.

The food is nothing short of incredible because Afghan food is elite, perioddddd. They also have a steaks menu. Ambiance is one for the books. Seriously. The interior design made us feel like our community DESERVES more like this!

Chicken is hand-slaughtered.

🌊☕ Brighton Beach, We’re Brewing Something Special! Moka & Co has officially opened its doors in the heart of Little Odessa, bringing the rich heritage of Yemeni coffee to the shores of Brooklyn.

Step inside for authentic flavors, warm hospitality, and a taste of the mountains that started it all. New York—your newest coffee escape has arrived at 403 Brighton Beach Ave Brooklyn, NY. 

#MokaAndCo #BrightonBeach #NYCcoffee #YemeniCoffee #LittleOdessa #BrooklynEats #CoffeeCulture

☕️✨ Light, aromatic, and beautifully spiced—Khaleeji Qahwah is unlike any other coffee in the world. Brewed with lightly roasted Yemeni Arabica beans, cardamom, and hints of saffron and cloves, it carries a golden color and a fragrance that feels adventurous.

For centuries, this coffee has welcomed guests across the Arabian Peninsula—served first, shared generously, and poured from the iconic dallah as a symbol of hospitality and respect.
One sip, and you’re tasting history. One pour, and you’re part of the tradition.

#Khaleeji #Qahwah #ArabicCoffee #MokaAndCo #ArabianHeritage #Gahwa #Arabica

✨ We’re delighted to announce the opening of Moka & Co – Brooklyn (Cortelyou Rd) at 1418 Cortelyou Rd in the heart of historic Ditmas Park — a neighborhood once gently rolling farmland that transformed into a leafy, suburban-in-the-city enclave in the early 1900s. 

This very street, Cortelyou Road, carries the legacy of Jacques Cortelyou, the 17th-century Dutch-Huguenot surveyor whose map-making helped shape New York’s colonial footprint. 

Join us for a moment of calm in the everyday — sip a traditionally brewed Yemeni coffee blend, feel the warmth of hospitality, and embrace the rich history nestled in our new home. We can’t wait to welcome you.

#brooklyncoffee #cortelyouroad #yemenicoffee #nyccoffee #organiccoffee #starbucks

latestPosts.caption:
Our Calabrese pie highlights some of Calabria’s most iconic ingredients and was inspired by a trip Dan Richer took many years ago. Traveling from town to town with a small group of chefs—visiting pasta makers, gelato shops, and farms—he developed a deep appreciation for the region’s flavors and producers. 

Applying what he learned on that trip, Dan set out to bring together Calabria’s signature flavors—chilis, ricotta, and onions—while using ingredients grown here in the U.S. The result is the Razza Calabrese: a pizza that honors the spirit of Calabria.

latestPosts.caption:
On this Christmas Eve, we’re grateful for all your support over the long year. This was a year of uncertainty, but I for one have come to rely on our whiskey audience for community, escape, and a sustaining energy that gives us all a reason to forge ahead into an unknown future.

We are open in the Navy Yard from 2pm to 8pm today and while we are closed tomorrow, we’re open regular hours until New Year’s Eve, when we’ll be open 2pm to 10pm, open New Year’s Day 12 to 8pm (with tours), and then ready to tackle 2026 with new ideas, new whiskeys, and new flavors. 

Until then we wish for you peace and joy, bolstered with a little whiskey, and we hope for happiness and health to all our friends, family, and neighbors. If this is in your feed, you mean a lot to us and we hope for the same from you. We wish you a happiest of New Year’s Day filled with hope and energy for a fresh start to 2026.

latestPosts.caption:
While some companies can promise delivery right until Christmas morning, we rely on retailers and partners around the country for legal compliance. We’re only allowed to direct-ship Whiskey to New York and a handful of states, so while we endeavor to send everything on time, we can no longer 100% promise customers in all states will get a bottle by the 25th if you order.

However, our new Whiskey Castle Card is a great next-best thing. It can be used for anything we sell in-person at the distillery from tours to merch to bottles to cocktails. It’s a great idea for anyone local to New York City or anyone planning to be local in the coming year.

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
✊🏼 They say “If you build it, they will come” and this past weekend we definitely built a home of love and solidarity at Columbus Park!! It was a sight to see and something to be proud of 🙏🏻

Thank you @jackliang and @mrbenwei @oliverpras for making this possible and @eastsidestoriesnyc for capturing all of this.

Huge shout out to one of the most talented videographers I know @oyuxi who captured this amazing 360 view of the whole event!!

I can’t express in words what it felt like to see our youth, community leaders, elders, families and folks from all different ethnicities come together as one. As I listened to @iammcjin @fungbros @nupol_justice @andrewyang @, nupal justice state senator @johnliuny talk about things that we all can do to make our communities a better place it reminded me that no matter how little we can all do our part 💯

As a result I am calling on all of my fellow restauranteurs and I know it’s been a challenging and tough time for all of us during the pandemic this past year to come together and create a night market and concert where 100 % of the proceeds will go to non-profits that will help the fight against HATE and support our elderly communities 🙌🏻

We are in the process of partnering up with @luckyricedotcom @jackliang and @thedaniellechang to bring this vision to life. If you’re interested in participating please leave a comment or DM us. This will be an event to remember as we celebrate LOVE through culture and food..

Please join us!!!!

latestIgtvVideos.title: It Takes A City! Support our Hometown Heroes!
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
A message from our founder @acewatanasuparp! - All of us have been affected either directly or indirectly, either a friend or a loved one, a neighbor or a co-worker from COVID-19 and it has nearly brought the “City that never sleeps” to a screeching halt. We say nearly, because this city is still moving! It’s moving on the back bone of essential workers all over the 5 boroughs.  They are our EMS, Healthcare workers, Police officers, MTA workers, Veterinary workers, supermarket workers, etc.

As a result we’ve created a Go Fund Me account called “It Takes a City” where all donations will be tax deductible and 100 percent of the proceeds will go towards feeding our heroic doctors and nurses and healthcare workers. This was made possible by our partnership with the “Bird and the Bear Foundation” EIN 84-2453073. The Bird and Bear Foundation is a 501(c) organization that started in 2018. 
This is a hard time for our country, especially our beloved city. We ask that if you’re able to donate please go to the link on our bio and help feed our brave men and woman who are on the front lines facing this pandemic every single day. With your help our goal is to help feed 800 meals a week 🙌🏻. Thank you for all your support and please stay safe and strong! #SpotDessertBar

we almost didn't make these.

red velvet felt too obvious for the holidays. but also... it's kind of always too sweet?

so someone said: "what if we put matcha inside it?"

we were like "there's no way that would work," but we tried it anyways. turns out, the bitterness cuts through the sweetness, perfectly balancing it.

then we went "love the color, what if we flipped it? matcha outside, red on the inside?" - so we took inspo from our best selling drink: Strawberry Matcha Latte

and that's how you get two unlikely holiday themed cookies.

Oh. My. Goodness. I don’t even know where to begin… @psarakinyc was absolutely INCREDIBLE! We’re in love with this restaurant. 😍 From the stunning waterfront skyline view of Manhattan to the warm hospitality of founder James, every moment was perfect. James made us feel completely at home, spending so much time explaining the story behind each dish and how to enjoy them authentically. After growing up in Greece from ages 6–19 and working in NYC’s restaurant scene for 33 years, he opened Psaraki in February 2024, and his passion shines through in every detail. He told us, “It’s not because I have to, it’s because I want to,” and it truly felt like he was hosting us in his own home.

We trusted James completely with our order, and he curated the perfect mix of dishes tailored to our tastes while encouraging us to try new things (which we all ended up loving). We started with a warm vegetable lemon soup, the coziest kickoff to a chilly night, followed by tuna tartar, hamachi, oysters, and scallops, all unbelievably fresh and light.

Appetizers included calamari, fish chips (which James showed us how to eat traditionally by hand!), octopus, horiatiki, and saganaki, every single one a standout. For drinks, we first let the bartender surprise us with sweet vodka-based cocktails, all AMAZING, then tried the spicy marg, pornstar martini, and Psaraki spritz, which were amazing.

For mains, we had lobster pasta, wood-grilled prawns, and branzino with fries, each bursting with authentic Greek flavor and SO GOOD! Dessert was the grand finale: bougatsa, Greek yogurt with sour cherry, baklava, and portokalopita (orange cake made with phyllo), paired with espresso martinis, Vin Santo dessert wine (aged under the sun and moon in Santorini), and mastiha as a digestif.

Between the flavors, the ambiance, and James’s heartwarming hospitality, it truly felt like we were on an exotic vacation in Greece. I didn’t want to leave or go back to reality, we already booked a reservation to come back this weekend! Every bite, sip, and moment was unforgettable. I HIGHLY recommend!! 🇬🇷🏛️🎏

📍Psaraki, Williamsburg

This dinner was AMAZING and some of the best Greek food we have had in the city!! 🇬🇷✨The service truly the best  and everyone made sure we were able to try all of their amazing dishes. We also loved having James host us he was so sweet!! 🥰🥰 Vibes inside were so cute and loved the view of the water and city 🌆 🌟OBSESSED with this place!!! 

What we tried 😋😋
🥂 Spicy mango margarita and aperol spritz
🐠 Fisherman’s experience - variety of apps, dips, and fried bites (we subbed for lamb chops, chicken, meatballs, and sausage) 
🍣 Scallops over rice mix 
🥗 Greek salad 
🥧 Galaktoboureko with ice cream

Shinjuku Station is officially on the move and they’re bringing their wildly popular Japanese street food right here to Winston! 🍜🍢 

From sushi burritos to sizzling yakitori skewers, their original spot has become a fan favorite… and now, Winston’s about to get a taste.

Get ready for:
🍣 Sushi rolls + burritos that actually live up to the hype

Shinjuku Station’s new Winston location is coming very soon and we’ll keep you posted. But for now, it’s worth the mini road trip 🚗💨

We’ve always known it — but now, it’s official: Italian cuisine is an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity! 

✨ This recognition by UNESCO celebrates not just the flavors, but the cultures that have shaped our understanding of food over the centuries.
 
For us, food is culture. It’s a mosaic of knowledge, dialogue, and influences that build bridges between people. This is the profound meaning of Italian cuisine as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity: affirming and sharing the values of intercultural exchange, culinary freedom, and gastronomic diversity.
 
At Eataly, we believe in a cuisine that unites, honors its roots, and is curious about the world. Every day in our stores, we celebrate the quality, the territories, the people, and the knowledge that make Italian cuisine a living, ever-evolving heritage — one to be preserved, passed on, and respectfully enriched.

Bombolone ✨🍫

A powdered-sugar dream — golden fried dough filled with luscious flavors like pistachio, dulce de leche, gianduja, and more!

Our holiday twist on this traditional Italian treat is not to be missed. Grab your Bombolone from our counters today!

One of the most iconic slices of New York is officially here.

@princestreetpizza opens its first permanent Miami location today, bringing its cult-favorite pepperoni squares and signature New York energy to the heart of @lincolnrd. 

The new shop marks the beloved brand’s long-awaited return to South Florida, following a wildly popular Wynwood pop-up that left locals craving more. CEO Lawrence Longo says the team is thrilled to finally plant roots in Miami Beach, promising the same “pure happiness” delivered at their famed NYC original.

“We are thrilled to open the doors of our first Miami brick-and-mortar location this December and to bring back our delicious slices to the South Florida community,” Lawrence shares.

Set at 521 Lincoln Road, the shop will serve the full lineup of Prince St. classics — from the iconic Spicy Spring™ to the Naughty Pie collab and a vegan favorite — all crafted with the brand’s signature scratch-made dough, fresh ingredients, and water filtration system designed to match New York’s. Guests can also grab housemade sauces, exclusive Miami-themed merch, and snap photos with a custom mural by local artist Bari-Lynn Friedlander. 

To celebrate opening day, the first 25 guests at noon will score a $25 gift card, with loyalty members entered to win free pizza for a year.

“Every bite and every interaction at our Lincoln Road location, similar to our other locations, will deliver pure happiness to our guests, and we look forward to being a part of such a bustling culinary scene.”

Head to the link in our bio for the full feature.

latestPosts.caption:
🍝 BRB, living my best life at ITA Kitchen! ✨

If you haven’t tried endless pasta night, you NEED this in your foodie rotation! Every Monday–Thursday they serve up chef’s choice pasta that rotates weekly, so it’s always fresh, always fun, and always worth going back for more. 🍷🍝

Let’s talk drinks 👇
🍸 That espresso martini sampler → chefs-kiss 😍
🍸 The rainbow cookie martini? A whole vibe 🌈
Perfect pairings with every pasta bite you take. 🍹

And OMG the ambience, think modern Italian vibes, cozy yet chic lighting, stylish decor, and music that keeps the energy right whether you’re on a date, a dinner night out, or celebrating something special. 💫
 
Whether you’re here for the pasta, the cocktails, or just that perfect Instagram moment, this spot hits every note. 🎶
 
📍 Garden City, NY

💡 Pro tip: go early weekday for a chill dinner mood or Friday/Sat for a livelier scene.

Forkfuls of happiness… unlimited. 🍝 Endless Pasta, Monday–Thursday, enjoy all the pasta you can eat. 🙌

Available in Garden City & Patchogue.

latestPosts.caption: I clearly love this place so much ⛵️⚓️🥂 #jerseycity #hoboken #nj #nyc

Would you go here ? The Willy Wall is the ultimate summer destination. It’s anchored in the New York Harbor near the Statue of Liberty. You get unobstructed views of the sunset and the city skyline. It has a Full bar and you can bring your own food .

The boat that takes you back and fourth from the Willy Wall leaves from the Manhattan Yacht club every 30 min.
📍140 Dudley st Jersey City 

It’s about a 16 min ride from the city if you take the PATH to Exchange Place or Grove St and then it’s about a 6 min walk . And the Light Rail is about a 1 min walk .

Our new wellness space on the White Island offers a holistic indoor–outdoor experience.
 
Last month, in partnership with @vuoriclothing, we hosted a five-day retreat centred on performance, recovery and connection to celebrate the opening of the Health Club. The Health Club features an indoor-outdoor gym with open-air training zones, a movement studio and a private PT area, along with a curated class schedule – from sunrise barre to our signature fascia and energy-release sessions.
 
Designed for deep recovery, the spa offers treatment huts, Omorovicza rituals, private onsen-style baths, and bookable contrast suites with ice baths and saunas.

House 44: our trackside home with Formula 1Ⓡ and Lewis Hamilton

This year, we teamed up with Lewis Hamilton and Formula 1 to launch House 44 - our dedicated pop-up suite inside the F1 Paddock Club™️ at Grand Prix weekends.

Members had the opportunity to go behind the scenes with guided track tours, paddock access, pit-lane walks, and priority access to podium celebrations. Plus, they enjoyed live performances and special guest appearances during the weekend.

latestPosts.caption:
Introducing ‘We Three Queens’ at Soho Farmhouse, by @jonathan_baldock⁠
 ⁠
‘We Three Queens’ uses Christmas as a starting point to explore Yule, queerness and nature. Baldock transforms the Nord with hanging tapestries, fairy-queen sculptures and a suspended Christmas tree. ⁠
 ⁠
Known for blending ritual, Paganism and queer perspectives, he reimagines the traditional carol through a non-heteronormative lens. Drawing on the rural setting, the installation reflects the cycle of the seasons. Each panel represents a season using sacred geometry; the inner sides spell ‘You Enrich This World’, a quote from Shon Faye highlighting the value of every individual.⁠
⁠
As part of the Step into the Blue series, in partnership with @bombaysapphireuk , we also hosted a workshop and talk with the Jonathan Baldock.⁠
 ⁠
The installation can be found in the Nord at Soho Farmhouse until Tuesday 30 December.

Taste America, presented by @capitalone, shines a light on the chefs and independent restaurants at the heart of our communities. Our TasteTwenty chefs are popping up around the country, hosting intimate dinners and walk-around tastings, and spreading the message of #GoodFoodForGood. 

Thank you to our sponsor @kerrygoldUSA for supporting local chefs and the work they do for their communities. Tap the link in our bio get tickets!

#ICYMI the James Beard House Fellows Program sponsored by @capitalone is back and better than ever. Applications for the 2022-2023 cohort are closing THIS Sunday, August 21! @ccapinc alums can apply now for a chance to participate in a ten-week residency that includes social media and leadership training, the opportunity to develop a meal kit in collaboration with @gpfood and much more. Visit the #linkinbio to apply and learn more about previous Fellows!

Today, we are excited to announce the 2022-2023 Legacy Network class of mentors and mentees. Founded in partnership with @woodfordreserve, the Legacy Network connects BIPOC industry veterans with the next generation to help build a more equitable future for hospitality and food media. 

Check out the new class by tapping the link in bio!

“There are three ways chefs impact the food system as changemakers: through the table, through community, [and] through policy.”—Anne E. McBride (@aemcbride), vice president of programs at the James Beard Foundation.

July marks the ten-year anniversary of our Chef Bootcamp for Policy and Change program. Since 2012, the program has continued to inspire and train chefs around the country to mobilize in support of policy decisions that impact our food system. Thank you to our sponsors, including @BestMadeCo, for supporting our efforts to build up the next generation of chef advocates. 

Applications for our fall 2022 Chef Bootcamp in Louisiana close this Sunday, July 17. Tap the link in our bio to apply now!

The application period for The James Beard Foundation's 2022 and 2023 WEL Cohorts is now open! 

The 10-week program created in conjunction with @cornelluniversity, is targeted to women owners of one or more restaurants or food businesses looking to expand and grow. 

The curriculum will address advanced business and finance concepts while also providing gender-specific training and leadership development. 

Learn more about the program at the JBF website and apply today! 

#JBFwomenlead #JBFchefslead #restaurants #womenentrepreneurs #womenleaders #businessgrowthstrategy

Busy Bee Cafe, @thebusybeeatl, in Atlanta, GA - 🏆 a 2022 JBF America's Classics winner! When Lucy Jackson opened the Busy Bee Café in1947, it was one of only two streets in the city of Atlanta open to Black entrepreneurs after the race riots pushed the community from downtown. Today, the cafe is owned by the Gates family with Tracy Gates at the helm, who keeps the cafe a community gathering spot and bastion of comforting soul food for generations past and present come to roost. 

For more stories like Busy Bee Cafe, tune into the 2022 #jbfa livestream on Twitter on Monday, June 13 at 5:30P.M. CT!

Introducing another 2022 America's Classics winner 🏆 - @casavegarestaurant in Sherman Oaks, CA where countless diners discover albondigas, enchiladas, sweet corn tamales, and tostadas! Founder, Rafael Vega, passed in 2021 from complications due to COVID-19, but his legacy lives on through his daughter and owner Christy who helps support the greater Latin American community in Los Angeles and beyond. Learn more about this America's Classic winner and make sure to tune into our livestream of the #jbfa Restaurant and Chef Awards on June 13 on Twitter!

On June 13th, it's time to #GatherForGood and celebrate the exceptional talent and achievement in the culinary arts at the 2022 #jbfa ceremony, sponsored by @acquapanna and @sanpellegrino_us. Join us on Twitter at 5:30 P.M. CT / 6:30 P.M. ET to watch the livestream.

Welcome to Solly’s Grille —  a #JBFA 2022 America’s Classic Winner and home to the iconic butter burger in Milwaukee Wisconsin! 🏆 Created in 1936 by Kenneth “Solly” Salmon, this sandwich features ground sirloin with stewed onions with the crowning glory of farm-fresh Wisconsin butter. It’s no surprise that people from far and wide make the pilgrimage to this family-owned restaurant that pays tribute to Wisconsin’s Dairy Heritage by using over 130 pounds of butter per week! 🐄🧈 @sollysgrille

Excited to share with you another #JBFA 2022 America’s Classic Winner 🏆 - @CorinnesPlace located in Camden, New Jersey. We’re more than impressed with everything on the menu from cajun-spiced turkey wings to the picnic-perfect black-eyed peas and of course the classic fried chicken! It’s not just the home-style soul food that we’re in awe of, but Corinne Bradley-Powers’ longevity as a business owner that remains a beacon of hope and continues to inspire!

James Beard House Fellows, presented by @capitalone, is a program that transforms the Beard House into a hub of training and professional development for talented emerging chefs. As part of the program, each Fellow will develop a Beard Box meal kit available for purchase and shipping across the continental U.S., as well as collaborate on exciting dinners at the Beard House.

Join us as we welcome our new 2022-2023 James Beard House Fellows: Jahqyad Austin (@jahqyad), Toni Hicks (@Teamtonii____), and Adijatu Jalloh (@a.m.jfusion and @adjis.kitchen ). Learn about our newest Fellows by tapping on the link in bio.

 #jbf #beardhousefellows #beardfoundation

Introducing Wo Hop — a #JBFA 2022 America's Classic Winner! 🏆 Wo Hop has been serving a distinct brand of Chinese American cuisine through a uniquely New York lens since 1938. Their "old-fashioned, chop-suey style food," as owner Ming Huang describes it, is a truly a timeless classic in the heart of the Chinatown, New York community and beyond! 🌃 🥡🍲 @wohop17 #JBF #WoHop #AmericasClassics

This Giving Tuesday, we're thinking about the places where birthdays are celebrated, friendships are forged, and customers and staff become regulars in each other's lives. Independent restaurants do more than serve great food—they preserve culinary traditions, drive innovation, and strengthen local food systems.

But right now, independent operators are facing an unprecedented amount of challenges, from rising costs to climate-related disasters. 

For nearly 40 years, we've championed the restaurants and people shaping American food culture. This #GivingTuesday, we're asking you to help us secure their future.

Tap the link in our bio to help us save Good Food. For Good.
